‘The diamond drill core and assays at Ilksan demonstrate the presence of a fertile copper porphyry system.’ Sarytogan Graphite managing director Sean Gregory According to Sarytogan, geological indicators such as elevated copper grades, potassic alteration and the presence of “B-veins”, a type of quartz vein commonly associated with porphyry copper systems, suggest the drilling is getting closer to the core of the porphyry system, where higher grades are typically found. At Ilksan, the B veins contain quartz, biotite, magnetite, potassium feldspar and chalcopyrite. Sarytogan Graphite managing director Sean Gregory said: “The diamond drill core and assays at Ilksan demonstrate the presence of a fertile copper porphyry system. The results of the deeper 3rd hole are eagerly anticipated.” The Ilksan discovery is the culmination of a systematic exploration campaign that began with a review of historical Soviet-era records. That work highlighted two shallow drill holes from the 1970’s that hit copper mineralisation, with grades reportedly increasing with depth. Since pegging the ground in 2024, the company has completed high-resolution magnetics, collected more than 6000 soil samples and conducted trenching, which returned a 270m-long intercept at 0.13 per cent copper. Subsequent shallow drilling then defined a 600m-diameter bedrock anomaly with grades up to 0.5 per cent copper, paving the way for the current deeper diamond drill campaign.

Advertisement

The move into copper appears to be a shrewd diversification play, leveraging the company’s established in-country exploration expertise and its deep knowledge of Kazakh permitting. The project sits in a region known for its mining prowess. Kazakhstan is a highly prospective jurisdiction for copper porphyry mines, with some of the world’s lowest-cost copper operations situated there, benefiting from low power, diesel and skilled labour costs. Elsewhere, just 25km to the northeast, recent testwork on a 24-tonne bulk sample of ore at Sarytogan’s flagship graphite deposit landed some eye-catching results. The test produced 30kg of coated spherical purified graphite (CSPG), delivering a hefty 97.7 per cent yield, eclipsing the typical industry range of 50 to 60 per cent. And perhaps more significantly, the end product reached a whopping 99.99 per cent purity, comfortably surpassing the typical 99.95 per cent lithium-ion battery requirement. The company is now preparing a 5kg sample of CSPG to ship to a leading European prototyping organisation. The material will be used to manufacture and test large format pouch cell batteries, a key step in qualifying the product for European offtake partners. With two long, consistent copper intercepts now in the bag, all eyes will likely be on the assays from the third and deepest hole of the program. That hole was drilled a further 150m north and terminated at 452m depth when the budget was exhausted.

Advertisement

If Sarytogan is right and it is indeed closing in on the high-grade core of this big porphyry system, the results from that deeper hole could make things very interesting very quickly for the Perth-based explorer. title: City of Perth faces yet another inquiry – this one, with teeth
text:
Advertisement

The City of Perth faces yet another inquiry as it battles to overcome “fractured working relationships” and “ongoing governance issues” plaguing the council. Local Government Inspector Tony Brown revealed the commencement of his formal inquiry after addressing councillors and city staff at a behind-closed-doors meeting on Monday evening, where he presented them with the findings of a five-month probe that began with the appointment of former Kwinana mayor Carol Adams as a monitor in January. Local Government Inspector Tony Brown outside the City of Perth’s Council House on Monday evening. Cameron Myles Brown told media the fresh inquiry would take about three months and cost about $120,000, however he was confident it would be a “short and effective way of providing an outcome for the City of Perth community”. The council has been in the headlines constantly this year after Adams was appointed to monitor the local government amid a relationship breakdown between councillors and the city administration.

Advertisement

Brown said Adams’ report was not a public document, however the inquiry report would be, and could include recommendations for the council to implement. “We could recommend to the minister for local government that the council be dismissed, or certain individuals be dismissed,” he said. “So that’s the worst-case scenario, and I do not want to pre-empt what the inquiry will find.” Legislatively, Brown cannot take action on Adams’ monitor’s report, which paved the way for his inquiry. Brown listed breaches of confidentiality, a breakdown of public working relationships, and city officers “inundated with way too many questions and requirements” as issues raised during the monitor’s inquiry.

Advertisement

Altogether, Adams’ report led to 12 actions that Brown made clear he expected the city to undertake. “The City of Perth is the flagship local government of Western Australia, so it needs to be the leader in governance,” he said. Related Article Local government Perth council blocks CEO return as investigation continues “I don’t think it’s there at the moment, so we’re going to work through that, and we want the City of Perth to be able to return to providing good governance for its community.” The local government inspector pushed back on suggestions bureaucracy was hindering meaningful action, noting the previous, well-publicised inquiry into the city ran for more than two years and cost $7 million, while his and Adams’ inquiries should be wrapped up within the space of nine to 12 months.

Advertisement

On Tuesday, Brown told ABC Perth he was not happy about issues in the ongoing relationships between elected members that had played out in the public arena, as well as the regular breaches of confidentiality. He said there had been a lot of complaints against councillors, both from within the city administration and the council itself, which showed the elected members were not working together well. “The working relationship between the council and the administration is the main focus, and you need to be working together,” he said. “And where we see individual elected members not wanting to work for their collective community and not wanting to build relationships, these sort of issues happen.” Opposition Leader Basil Zempilas – who was previously the Perth lord mayor before his elevation to state politics – said he was “genuinely disappointed” about the state of affairs at his old council, which he said had worked hard to act on the lessons from the previous inquiry.

Advertisement

“To see the city be back in a position where its reputation is being questioned is deeply distressing to me because I know how hard myself, the new council, and the administration worked together to change that position,” he said on Tuesday morning. “We worked incredibly hard, harmoniously, and always put the ratepayers of the City of Perth first.” City of Perth chief executive Michelle Reynolds was suspended by the council in May after councillors and city staff received a briefing on Adam’s report from Brown, during which he put the council “on notice” regarding the monitor’s probe. The development prompted an angry response from Local Government Minster Hannah Beazley who in turn raised the spectre of council amalgamations. Last month, a motion to bring Reynolds back from suspension “effective immediately” was voted down, with councillors opting to defer the decision until after the completion of a workplace culture review.

Advertisement

Zempilas said the question of Reynolds’ employment situation “does not appear to be answered”, and warned against a situation where the inquiry “drags on and drags on”. “It is incumbent upon councils to work together in the best interests of the ratepayers, and clearly there has been a breakdown here,” he said. “And I’ve got to say, as the capital city for Western Australia, everyone has a right to feel disappointed about what’s taken place there.” Opposition local government spokeswoman Kirrilee Warr questioned the need for another inquiry, declaring: “This has been going on for far too long.” “Hopefully we can get to the bottom of what’s going on at the City of Perth,” she said.

Advertisement

Warr initially held hope that recent reforms that led to the creation of the local government inspector’s office would make a difference in the sector, but now has her doubts. “I think this Labor government hasn’t been clear with local government around what is the plan,” she said. “They are very good to drop hot minute statements across media or in forums to lead people down a path to think that there will be a result, but right now we are seeing a number of councils being called in once again around their behaviours, around relationships, and around how they’re conducting themselves, and that is not good for anyone.” The City of Perth was the first council to be allocated a monitor, just two weeks into Brown’s role as the head local government watchdog at the start of the year.

US rapper Macklemore says he was dropped as the support act for Ed Sheeran’s American tour after making pro-Palestine comments on stage this month. The Thrift Shop rapper stood by his “Free Palestine” comments, made during a performance at New Jersey’s MetLife Stadium this month, in a detailed Instagram post that attracted criticism from a US-based pro-Israel activist group and the singer Pink. Macklemore has been dropped from Ed Sheeran’s tour after onstage support for Palestine. Getty In the post, Macklemore said Sheeran had told him that New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft called him to say Macklemore was banned from performing in a stadium owned by his business group. “Ed also told me that Kraft had rallied some of the other stadium owners, and collectively they gave him an ultimatum: if Macklemore stays on the tour, you will not be allowed to play in our venues,” Macklemore said in the post.

Advertisement

Sheeran, who is a famously apolitical artist, was forced to pick a side. While Macklemore says the pair remain friends, how did this controversy arise? Who is Macklemore? The Grammy Award-winning artist, whose real name is Benjamin Haggerty, broke records with his 2013 hit Thrift Shop with Ryan Lewis and featuring Wanz, becoming the second independently distributed song to reach number one on Billboard’s Hot 100. It came off the back of 2012 hit Same Love – also with Lewis – supporting same-sex relationships and marriage equality, three years before the US legalised it.

Advertisement

Known for independently producing and distributing his music, Macklemore has never been coy about his advocacy. When he sang at the NRL grand final in 2017, he called for marriage equality during an emotional performance one month before it was legalised in Australia. On Tuesday morning (AEST), the artist said via Instagram, after he was barred from Sheeran’s Loop tour of North America, that he had expressed support on stage for Palestine for the past three years. Macklemore, performing in Dublin last year, has proclaimed “Free Palestine” on stage. Redferns “What I said at MetLife, I have been saying on stages around the world for almost three years. So why is it an issue now?” Macklemore said, adding that he believed his comments during concerts had become a “resistance” and thus it “became so important to silence me”. “I’m sharing a stage with one of the biggest artists in the world, in some of the biggest stadiums in America. At a certain level of exposure, ‘Free Palestine’ becomes too much of a risk. If I kept doing the shows, saying Free Palestine, with Ed implicitly supporting it, the crowd getting loud and showing undeniable support for Palestinian liberation, what artist might speak out next?”

Advertisement

Sheeran has not commented, and a replacement opening act for his tour is yet to be confirmed. How did we get here? The controversy began at MetLife Stadium on September 4, during his support spot for Sheeran, when Macklemore exclaimed “Free Palestine” while introducing his protest song Hind’s Hall, and showed footage of the devastation in Gaza on a screen. Macklemore and Ed Sheeran, pictured in 2014, have been longtime friends. Getty Written after the 2024 campus protests supporting Palestinians, the song is named for Hind Rajab, a five-year-old Palestinian girl who was killed after Israeli forces opened fire on her family’s car in Gaza City. (Macklemore also performed the song during his 2024 tour of Australia.)

Advertisement

Related Article Gaza Strip She was five years old and under fire. In this film, we hear her last words “A big part of the reason why I wanted to do this tour in the first place is so that I could stand up in stadiums like this and say two words that are very, very dear to my heart: Free Palestine,” Macklemore said during the performance in New Jersey. The following night, he returned to the stage and said: “To all of my Jewish brothers and sisters, criticism of Israel, criticism of apartheid, being against genocide, it in no way is criticism of you. “This message is for peace, love, for all human beings to be treated with dignity, respect, and equality.” In his Instagram post, Macklemore said he held no ill-will toward Sheeran, whom he considered a friend of 13 years. “As I told Ed multiple times on the phone, our friendship can’t change my responsibility to tell the truth about what happened,” Macklemore wrote.

Advertisement

Despite this, the controversy has wedged Sheeran into a position where he must make a political choice – as an apolitical singer. “Ed was in a f---ed-up position. He knew it. His typical apolitical stance was being challenged in a way it never had been before,” Macklemore said on Instagram. Sheeran performing at Melbourne’s Marvel Stadium in February during his Loop tour. Richard Clifford “He told me that the words ‘Free Palestine’ and the image of the Palestinian flag were hurtful to a lot of people he spoke with. “I told him that if those words were more offensive than tens of thousands of Palestinian children being killed by Israel, then there was a fundamental disconnect between where those people stood and where I stood. But he couldn’t get past his public-facing ‘don’t take sides’.”

Advertisement

A growing chorus of organisations and experts say Israel’s wartime actions in Gaza amount to genocide – an accusation Israel vehemently rejects. Pink and other critics lash out Macklemore’s tour comments drew criticism from fellow singer Pink, who is Jewish. She then attracted backlash herself. Singer Pink criticised Macklemore’s performance in New Jersey. AP “Last weekend [Macklemore] stood in front of a stadium full of music-loving families, with violent images from a war on the screens, dedicated a song to the movement of his choice, and then took the mic to tell all of the Jews in the stadium that it wasn’t about them,” Pink said.

Advertisement

Sydney live reviews Macklemore brings Gaza protest song to Sydney “You don’t get to decide that for us.” Pink also pointed out that in 2014, Macklemore apologised for a costume he wore which included a black wig, beard and a fake hooked nose, which critics labelled antisemitic. Macklemore addressed Pink’s comments in his Instagram post, saying the real victims were Palestinian people “who have been killed, starved, displaced and forced to live through unimaginable violence”. His post on Tuesday attracted support from activist Greta Thunberg, Irish band Kneecap, British singer Bob Vylan – who have each expressed support publicly for the Palestinian cause – and the Australian singer-songwriter Tones and I, who is friends with Macklemore and has collaborated with him previously.

Advertisement

US-based campaign group StopAntisemitism criticised Macklemore after his recent performances, saying “Jewish fans bought tickets to see Ed Sheeran sing ... [and] not to be ambushed by Macklemore’s anti-Israel propaganda”. According to its website, StopAntisemitism reaches nearly “one billion” people and transforms “awareness into action and advocacy into measurable change, including hundreds of firings, suspensions, expulsions, and arrests”. Who is Robert Kraft? Among the venues to bar Macklemore is Gillette Stadium – home to the NFL’s New England Patriots – in Foxborough, Massachusetts, south of Boston. Robert Kraft, the billionaire owner of the NFL team and stadium, said the decision to cancel Macklemore was a result of his recent comments “and a broader history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery that we believe has been deeply offensive and hurtful to the Jewish community”.

Advertisement

Robert Kraft, the owner of the New England Patriots. Getty Images “This decision is not about diminishing the suffering of innocent Palestinians or denying anyone the right to advocate on their behalf. Their pain and loss are real,” Kraft said in a statement Monday. Macklemore’s advocacy “should not come at the expense of the Jewish community or obscure the responsibility of Hamas”, Kraft said. The tour’s promoter, Messina Touring Group, said in a statement to Rolling Stone that venues had notified it that “they will not allow a concert to take place with Macklemore on the line-up, which would result in the cancellation of the tour and impact hundreds of thousands of fans”. Macklemore had been scheduled to perform at several stadiums owned by NFL-affiliated groups as part of Sheeran’s tour.

Related Article War Are we in World War III, and just don’t know it? While Macklemore did not name other stadiums that decided to bar him from performing, earlier this year, Ye – best known by his former name, Kanye West – performed in Los Angeles’ SoFi Stadium (home to the Los Angeles Rams and the Los Angeles Chargers) and Florida’s Raymond James Stadium (home to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers). This was despite Ye’s long history of antisemitic remarks, praise of Adolf Hitler and the selling of merchandise depicting swastikas. title: Truck owner cops $2,091 fine after bizarre excuse for illegal dumping: 'Creative but not convincing'
text:
A truck driver has been fined $2,091 after dumping demolition waste in Melbourne's north, before giving the state's Environment Protection Authority a bizarre explanation.

Last month, the man was found to have illegally dumped a skip bin-sized load of rubbish next to Oatlands Road in Bulla.

Seemingly thinking he would drive off, the truck driver was bogged less than 50 metres from the mound of demolition waste he had just left.

Advertisement Advertisement

Advertisement Advertisement

The waste pile was measured by EPA officers and found to be the same size as the skip bin on the back of the bogged truck.

A further discovery showed scraps of material matching the pile were still in the bin.

But despite the evidence, the man denied he or the vehicle had any connection to the dumping.

Hume City councillor Naim Kurt has welcomed the crackdown on illegal dumping. Source: Facebook/Naim Kurt

Truck owner fined over alleged waste dumping

EPA North Metropolitan Regional Manager Steve Riley said the driver insisted he hadn't been driving before mysteriously leaving in an Uber.

"While it was a creative explanation, it was not a convincing one. We have fined the registered owner of the truck and ordered them to clean up the waste. If they don't comply, they will face further fines and enforcement actions," he said in a statement.

Advertisement Advertisement

Advertisement Advertisement

"Illegal dumping is too big a problem for any one regulator or agency to solve on its own, but working together we can make a huge difference."

The truck's owner has now been fined $2,091 for unlawful deposit of waste under Section 115 of the Environment Protection Act.

They were handed a Waste Abatement Notice requiring them to take the waste to a facility licensed to receive it.

Advertisement Advertisement

Hume City Council councillor Naim Kurt said this case sent a clear message to people considering illegally dumping waste.

"The message is clear. If you dump, you will be caught, fined and held to account," Kurt said.

Over $20m spent on cleaning up illegal dumping

The Victorian EPA revealed that illegal dumping costs communities millions each year, as the state government commits $21.5 million to tackling the problem.

EPA Executive Director of Operations Rachel Gualano told Yahoo News Victorians are sick of "environmental criminals".

"EPA Victoria is taking action to detect, catch and disrupt them, execute strong enforcement action and make them clean up their mess," she said.

Growing issue across Melbourne

The latest case of illegal dumping in Melbourne's north resonates with rubbish removalist Josh who runs Northern Rubbish Removals. He has noticed the problem worsening in recent years.

Josh from Northern Rubbish Removal feels like illegal dumping is getting worse each year across Melbourne. Source: Supplied

"There's definitely a lot of illegal dumping," he said.

Advertisement Advertisement

Advertisement Advertisement

"From Craigieburn to Mickleham, all the way down through Wollert, Kalkallo, it's just littered with illegal dumping.

"People find like a dark secluded area, dump it, and just expect the councils to pick it up."

The issue continues to spread across Victoria, with the EPA receiving 3,744 reports of illegal dumping in 2024-25, almost double the figure recorded two years earlier.
